recommendation.reason: Two funeral destinations and five wedding destinations are seven named destination lookups, but the currently supported flower-buying decisions collapse into three coherent intents: condolence, wedding congratulations, and office opening/moving. Address/floor/operator differences deserve prominent sections and direct anchors; they do not yet support seven separately expanded 2,500–3,000-character buying guides. N3 reduces repeated product/policy/order paragraphs while preserving all facility-name queries. This is a content-design judgment, not evidence of search volume or a ranking prediction.
recommendation.importantFraming: The sender normally already knows the destination from the obituary or invitation. Do not turn either grouped guide into a ranking or a venue-selection comparison. Help locate the named destination and choose a flower product, ribbon and consultation path.

alternativeAssessment.reason: All five wedding candidates share four congrats SKUs, the same cost/fulfilment limits and the same main purchase questions. Verified venue detail is mostly address, hall name/floor and general access. Separate long pages would invite thin destination swaps or emotional padding. Official flower acceptance differences, materially different order processes or other independent decision evidence have not been established.

Wedding consolidation is well founded. The same test also applies to the two funeral pages: one has multiple official room floors; the other is an externally operated B2 funeral hall. These facts are useful, but do not establish different product, budget, ribbon, deadline, or fulfilment decisions. Calling one hospital a university hospital and the other local, or assigning different social relationships, would not create unique buying value. Two separate pages could be reconsidered only if future original evidence supports genuinely distinct decisions.
